name: Technique - Drift filter movement and pitch FM
description: Standalone technique from the Ableton Drift checklist: Env 2 low-pass movement, audio-rate LFO pitch FM, inverse high-pass and Saturator.

manual.instruction: Initialize Drift: turn oscillator 2 down, remove filter modulation, set Envelope 1 sustain to 100% and release to minimum, and set velocity-to-volume to 0%.
manual.verify: The synth is a clean saw through an open low-pass with no hidden modulation.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler starts from an initialized Drift.

manual.instruction: Set the low-pass near 20 Hz, assign Envelope 2 to filter frequency, raise attack, drop sustain to 0% and adjust decay until it opens and closes like a wub.
manual.verify: The filter moves slowly enough to read as a growl, not a pluck.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler uses Envelope 2 on the low-pass with slow attack and zero sustain.

manual.instruction: Set Drift's LFO to 1:1 so it runs at audio rate. Apply a small amount to pitch and choose a whole-number ratio from 1 to 16.
manual.verify: The growl gains aggressive FM harmonics while staying tonal.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler uses Drift's 1:1 LFO for pitch FM with whole-number ratios.

manual.instruction: Assign Envelope 2 negatively to the high-pass so it moves opposite the low-pass, then use Envelope 2 to control the LFO amount.
manual.verify: The filter tone evolves through the note rather than sitting still.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler adds inverse high-pass movement and envelope-controlled LFO depth.

manual.instruction: Add Saturator after Drift, increase drive, try Base Shape or Color modes, and keep width/unison modest.
manual.verify: The growl is louder and more aggressive but still mono-compatible in the low end.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler uses Saturator's drive, Base Shape and Color, then discusses width and unison.

notes: Source: Matt Tinkler, 'Make AWESOME Bass Growls With Ableton Drift' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KQlGU3LTWMk). Transcript summary, not quotes. Reference-only because the engine cannot create or verify Drift patches.
